chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Habeeb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, and with the seller were two slaves. So he said to the buyer, 'Go with both of them and choose whichever you wish, and return the other,' and he had taken the money. So the buyer went with both of them, and one of them absconded from his presence.

He said: Let him return the one who is still with him and take back half the price from what he gave to the seller, and go in search of the slave. If he finds him, he can choose whichever of the two he wishes and return the half money which he had taken; and if he does not find him, the slave is shared between them, half for the seller and half for the buyer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one of two slaves sold together absconds before the buyer chooses?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *Khiyar al-Majlis* (option of the meeting) in a conditional sale, ruling that the buyer must return the remaining slave and reclaim half the price to pursue the missing one. If the absconded slave is not recovered, the remaining slave becomes a joint property (*Musha*) between seller and buyer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of preserving equity when the specific object of sale is uncertain. This ruling underscores the importance of clear ownership division in cases of partial performance and loss within commercial contracts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Habeeb, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bought a slave from a man, and with him were two slaves.

So he said to the buyer, ‘Go with them both and choose whichever you so desire to, and return the other’, and he had taken the money. So the buyer went with both of them, and one of them absconded from his presence.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him return the one who is still with him and take back half the money from what he had given from the transaction, and he should go in seeking the slave. So if he were to find him, he can choose whichever of the two he so desires to and return the half money which he had taken; and if he does not find him, the slave would be between the two of them, half for the seller and half for the buyer’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Habib from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who buys a slave from another man who had two slaves and he says to the buyer, Take both of them then choose whichever you like and return the other’ and he has received payment. The buyer takes both of them but one of them runs away from the location of the buyer.

He (the Imam) said, ‘He must return the one with him and take half of the price he has paid, then search for the runaway slave. If he finds him he then chooses either one that he likes and returns the other. If he does not find him the slave belongs to both of them in the manner of equal shares.’”
